title: FDA: Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA) overview page

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

source_type: Government agency web page (content current as of 10/29/2026 per page)
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency (FDA) is also the party administering the requirement.
findings: Lists new industry requirements: serious adverse event reporting within 15 business days; facility registration with renewal every two years; product listing with annual updates; safety substantiation records.
States: "Neither the law nor FDA regulations require specific tests to demonstrate the safety of individual products or ingredients."

States MoCRA exempts certain small businesses from GMP, registration, and product listing requirements, with the exemptions not applying to eye-contact, injected, internal-use or more-than-24-hour appearance-altering products.

Notes GMP and fragrance allergen labeling regulations are still to be established by FDA (a draft GMP guidance is listed); a proposed talc-asbestos testing rule from December 2024 is listed as withdrawn in November 2025.
limitations: Agency summary page, not the statute; page content may change after the access date.
Publication date not stated; "content current as of" 10/29/2026 recorded in findings only.
Pending GMP rulemaking details and compliance dates were not read.
